case.summary: Case HHG-014 has been classified as fraud with a calibrated probability of 0.86, driven by a high-risk device fingerprint tied to multiple confirmed fraud cases and a large connected device component. The transaction occurred online via a new device behind an anonymous proxy, carrying account takeover characteristics that heavily outweighed features like the initial low model risk score. Furthermore, the customer explicitly denied making the transaction, cementing the fraudulent nature of the activity after an initial posterior score of 0.403. In response to these findings, the policy engine has executed automated safeguards to block the card, create a formal case, file a regulatory report, and monitor connected cards.

sar.narrative:
Suspicious Activity Report Narrative:

Case ID HHG-014 involves unauthorized card-not-present activity resulting in a financial exposure of $187.33. The fraudulent transaction was executed online via an anonymous proxy using a device flagged as new to the card. Technical indicators associate the device with a Tier 4 risk classification, which includes 74 other cards within the observation window and four confirmed prior fraud cases linked to the same hardware profile. Graph network analysis further places the device within a wider structural component comprising 5,487 cards and 9,199 narrow devices exhibiting high-velocity transaction volumes. The customer explicitly denied authorizing the transaction upon review. Consequently, the card was blocked and scheduled for reissue, and the activity has been classified as confirmed fraud under case HHG-014.
